claims: Environment Agency LIDAR Composite DTM 1m is a raster elevation model covering about 99 percent of England.
the 1m product represents terrain after surface objects are removed from the DSM.
surface-object removal uses bespoke algorithms and manual editing.
the composite is derived from Time Stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
where repeat surveys exist the newest best-resolution data is selected.
resampled source data uses bilinear interpolation before merging.
the documented 2022 composite includes surveys from 6 June 2000 to 2 April 2022.
metadata index catalogues identify which survey contributed at a location.
1m data is delivered as GeoTIFF rasters.
download tiles are 5km and aligned to the OS National Grid.
elevation values are in metres.
vertical reference is Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
the composite uses the OSTN15 transformation method.
individual contributing surveys are documented with plus or minus 15cm RMSE vertical accuracy.
the dataset coordinate reference system is EPSG:27700.
the dataset has no public access constraint and uses the Open Government Licence.
the 1m metadata record exposes WMS, WCS, WMTS, WFS metadata and OGC API Features links.
WMS is for visualised or summarised elevation, not authoritative numeric sampling.
WCS supplies elevation coverage suitable for numeric raster readback.
Esri image services were replaced by open-standard WCS and WMS services.
current service naming removes release-year suffixes to support future updates.
WCS GeoTIFF NoData is documented as -3.4028235e+38.
NoData pixels must not be interpreted as real elevations.
survey download packages now include spatial metadata index files in GeoPackage format.
metadata index files describe spatial location and temporal extent of elevation data.
Time Stamped products provide survey-specific dates and resolutions.
Time Stamped products can be available at 25cm, 50cm, 1m and 2m resolutions.
Time Stamped data uses transformation and geoidal models specific to the survey period.
the metadata catalogue is required to identify survey date, resolution, transformation and geoid.
DTM is distinct from DSM because DSM includes vehicles, buildings and vegetation.
first-return DSM is distinct from last-return DSM and terrain DTM.
first-return DSM coverage need not match last-return composite coverage.
the 2m DTM follows the same composite lineage and 5km GeoTIFF delivery model.
the 10m DTM is resampled from the 2m composite using bilinear interpolation.
10m DTM is a different product resolution and must not be substituted for 1m candidate sampling without explicit methodology.
metadata record revision and survey period are separate concepts.
annual update frequency does not prove every location has a recent survey.
about 99 percent national coverage does not guarantee coverage at a specific candidate point.
survey-age variation must be retained in candidate provenance.
interpolation can alter sampled values relative to source-resolution measurements.
vertical RMSE is a survey quality metric and not an error bound for a derived height difference without propagation.
candidate numeric extraction requires exact WCS or raster bytes for the target point.
candidate extraction must use EPSG:27700 coordinates or a verified transformation.
tile name TQ29SE alone does not prove the target pixel is present and valid.
metadata FeatureServer reports spatial reference 27700 and a maximum record count.
FeatureServer query metadata is not a substitute for DTM raster elevation values.
ground-truth surveys use independently surveyed points to verify timestamped LIDAR accuracy.
ground-truth points are documented at about plus or minus 3cm RMSE.
LIDAR surveys must satisfy published RMSE and random-error quality controls.
exact TQ2892 filtered metadata and numeric raster readback remain required before promotion.
